title: bug: on Windows the daemon's bare `git` execFile with cwd=<project> runs a repository git.exe
description:
util/diskState.ts defaultGitRunner (claim_next_task/release_task computeDiskStateSignature) and util/cachedPlanPaths.ts runGit/runGitHead call execFile('git', …, { cwd: <project> }); on Windows libuv searches the spawn cwd before PATH, so a git.exe/git.com committed at the project root runs as the daemon user — this bypasses the IDE-side protected runtime selection (CQ-R01 pins only the daemon's own working directory, not explicit spawn cwds).
Verified 2026-10-25, node v24.16.0 / libuv 1.52.1: whoami.exe copied to <cwd>\git.exe ran for execFile('git', [], { cwd }) both with NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath unset and =1 (real git: 2.54.0.windows.1).
Fix: resolve git once to an absolute path from PATH, skipping cwd, blank and relative entries (as accounts/claudeAuth.ts findWindowsCommand does), and execFile that path from every runner; also check diskState's runner, which lacks cachedPlanPaths' readOnlyGitEnv/readOnlyGitArgs config masking.
definitionOfDone: On Windows no daemon git runner executes a git.exe/git.com from the spawn cwd or a blank/relative PATH entry; a Windows-only test plants <cwd>/git.exe and proves the PATH git runs instead.
diskState defaultGitRunner and cachedPlanPaths runGit/runGitHead share the one resolved absolute git; POSIX behaviour is unchanged.
Fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
Add the shared git resolver and its cross-platform unit tests.

New packages/moe-daemon/src/util/gitExecutable.ts:
- `export function resolveGitExecutable(platform: NodeJS.Platform, pathValue: string, isFile: (file: string) => boolean = <fs.statSync(file).isFile() in try/catch, false on error>): string`.
  - platform !== 'win32': return 'git' WITHOUT probing (POSIX unchanged, execvp does the PATH lookup).
  - win32: split pathValue on ';', trim each entry, strip one pair of surrounding double quotes (as accounts/claudeAuth.ts findWindowsCommand does). Use an entry ONLY when fully qualified: drive-absolute (`X:\` / `X:/`) or UNC (`\\host...` / `//host...`), e.g. /^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|[\\/]{2}[^\\/])/. Skip blank, relative (`.`, `bin`, `.\tools`), drive-relative (`C:tools`) and root-relative (`\tools`, `/tools`) entries: libuv resolves those against the spawn cwd, i.e. the project.
  - Per entry, in PATH order, probe path.win32.join(dir, 'git.com') then 'git.exe' (libuv's order). Do NOT use PATHEXT: libuv only runs .com/.exe today, and Node refuses a .cmd/.bat without a shell (EINVAL).
  - Error handling: on a miss, throw Object.assign(new Error('git.com or git.exe not found in any fully qualified PATH entry'), { code: 'ENOENT' }). Never fall back to the bare name on win32. The stat probe swallows only its own per-candidate errors.
- `export function gitExecutable(): string`: module-level `let resolved: string | undefined`; `return (resolved ??= resolveGitExecutable(process.platform, process.env.PATH ?? ''))`. Lazy, never at module load (a missing git must not break the import). A success is cached for the process and shared by every runner; a throw leaves it unset, so a later call retries (git installed after daemon start).
- Short header comment with the why: on Windows libuv looks for a bare name in the spawn cwd (.com, .exe) before PATH, ignoring NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath, and resolves relative PATH entries against that cwd, so execFile('git', ..., { cwd: project }) ran a repository-committed git.exe as the daemon user (measured node 24.16 / libuv 1.52.1). Every daemon git spawn must use gitExecutable(). CQ-R01's IDE-side PATH filtering does not cover the spawn cwd.

New packages/moe-daemon/src/util/gitExecutable.test.ts. These run on every OS (CI runs daemon tests on ubuntu only), with an injected recording isFile and exact assertions:
(a) 'linux' and 'darwin' return 'git' and never call isFile.
(b) win32, PATH `;  ;.;bin;.\tools;C:tools;\tools;/tools;"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd";D:\later`, isFile always true: returns exactly 'C:\\Program Files\\Git\\cmd\\git.com', and the recorded probes equal exactly that one path, so no skipped entry was ever probed.
(c) PATH `C:\a;C:\b`, where only C:\a\git.exe and C:\b\git.com exist: returns C:\a\git.exe, and the probes are exactly [C:\a\git.com, C:\a\git.exe]. PATH order comes first, then .com before .exe within a folder.
(d) A UNC `\\srv\tools` entry and a forward-slash `c:/git/cmd` entry are accepted, with the expected path.win32.join outputs.
(e) win32 with an empty PATH, and with only relative entries plus isFile always true: throws an error whose code is 'ENOENT'. Assert the code, and that nothing is returned.
implementationPlan.note: Added gitExecutable.ts (resolveGitExecutable + lazy cached gitExecutable) and gitExecutable.test.ts cases (a)-(e) plus a directory-named-git.exe case; 10 tests pass in a Linux snapshot (/tmp/moe-d72f-gate.*, MOE_* unset). 531 other dirty paths in the shared checkout belong to peers; untouched. start_step hit a transient EPERM on the task json rename once, retry succeeded.

implementationPlan.description:
Route all three daemon git runners through gitExecutable(), then prove it on mocked and real Windows spawns. (gitExecutable.test.ts already exists from step 1; it is listed in newFiles only because it is not on disk at plan time.)

- util/diskState.ts defaultGitRunner: `execFileAsync(gitExecutable(), args, {same options})`. Error handling: the call stays inside the async runner, so a resolution miss rejects and computeDiskStateSignature still returns undefined (invariant 1). Rewrite its doc comment to say two things:
  - It spawns the shared absolute git.
  - It deliberately does NOT adopt cachedPlanPaths' readOnlyGitEnv/readOnlyGitArgs. This answers the task's 'also check diskState's runner'. Masking global/system config (core.excludesFile ignores, Git for Windows' system core.autocrlf) changes which paths `git status` lists. That lets the equality-only signature flap and raise false stale alarms, which invariant 1 forbids, and it would change POSIX behaviour, which the DoD says must stay the same. The absolute path already closes the binary-planting vector.
  - Keep GIT_STATUS_ARGS and every other option byte-identical.
- util/cachedPlanPaths.ts runGit and runGitHead: replace 'git' with gitExecutable() INSIDE the existing try blocks; runGitHead keeps its maxBytes check first. Error handling: a miss is then handled exactly like a spawn ENOENT:
  - runGit rethrows it (it is not the config exit-1 case);
  - runGitHead rethrows it (the code is not numeric);
  - openProjectGit names it in the miss.
  - repositorySource.ts and requiredChecks.ts inherit the fix with no edits.
- src/util/cachedPlanPaths.test.ts already mocks node:child_process. Add vi.mock('./gitExecutable.js') with a hoisted vi.fn that returns the sentinel 'C:\\Program Files\\Git\\cmd\\git.exe', and restore that implementation after each test.
  - New test: runGit, runGitHead and diskState's defaultGitRunner (imported from './diskState.js') each spawn exactly the sentinel (execFileMock.mock.calls[i][0]). diskState's call keeps its own args unchanged and passes no env option.
  - New test: when gitExecutable throws {code:'ENOENT'}, findCachedPlanPaths returns a miss containing 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel: ENOENT:'. computeDiskStateSignature(root) resolves undefined. runGitHead rejects with that error. execFileMock is never called, so there is no bare-name fallback.
  - Existing tests stay unchanged and green.
- src/util/gitExecutable.test.ts has no mocks, so real spawns. Add describe.runIf(process.platform === 'win32') with it.each(['git.exe','git.com']):
  - mkdtemp a cwd under os.tmpdir() and copy %SystemRoot%\System32\whoami.exe to <cwd>\<name>.
  - Assert gitExecutable() passes path.win32.isAbsolute and is not under cwd.
  - Assert defaultGitRunner(['--version'], cwd), runGit(['--version'], cwd, 10_000) and runGitHead(['--version'], cwd, 10_000, 4096) (stdout as utf8) each match /^git version /.
  - rmSync the cwd in finally/afterEach.
  - Old code using a bare 'git' runs the planted whoami copy. whoami rejects --version, so the test is red on the old code.
implementationPlan.note: diskState.defaultGitRunner, cachedPlanPaths.runGit and runGitHead now spawn gitExecutable() inside their existing try/async scope; diskState args/options byte-identical, no readOnly env adoption (rationale in its doc comment). cachedPlanPaths.test.ts: vi.mock('./gitExecutable.js') sentinel + 2 new tests (sentinel spawn, ENOENT miss/no fallback). gitExecutable.test.ts: Windows-only describe.runIf real-spawn block (git.exe/git.com planted whoami). Linux snapshot: 3 util files 67 passed | 2 skipped (the Windows-only cases).

implementationPlan.description:
Verification, run once. The exact command is `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test`. It must exit 0, and its fresh output tail is the complete_task verification evidence.
- The shared checkout's node_modules is a Windows install: never npm install or run vitest in /mnt/d.
- Run the command in an isolated Linux snapshot:
  - start from a HEAD archive, copy your 5 files over and cmp them;
  - symlink the native Linux node_modules (memory gotcha-linux-vitest-reuse-native-node-modules);

- In the same snapshot:

- Then run src/util/gitExecutable.test.ts and src/util/cachedPlanPaths.test.ts on Windows-native node from a %TEMP% copy (memory pattern-qa-windows-native-vitest-from-wsl), with --reporter=verbose. Confirm both planted cases (git.exe, git.com) RAN and passed, not skipped. That run is DoD 1's evidence, because CI runs daemon tests only on ubuntu.
- Record the suite counts, both tsc exit codes and the Windows result in the step note.
implementationPlan.note: Verification in an isolated Linux snapshot (HEAD archive + my 5 files, cmp-identical, native Linux node_modules symlink, MOE_* unset). `npm test` with a Linux-only PATH: exit 0, 167 files passed, 4219 passed | 16 skipped. (With the inherited Windows PATH one accounts/cli.test.ts case fails with the documented Windows-dir PATH env issue, unrelated to this task.) `npx tsc --noEmit` (package) exit 0; test-file typecheck for gitExecutable.test.ts + cachedPlanPaths.test.ts exit 0 (needed --types node). Windows-native node 24.16 from %TEMP% copy, --reporter=verbose: gitExecutable/cachedPlanPaths/diskState tests 3 files, 69 passed, 0 skipped; both planted cases ('runs the PATH git, not a git.exe/git.com in the cwd') RAN and passed.

Adversarial review, no code change after step 3 (5 files cmp-identical to the verified snapshot, so no rerun needed). Mutation probes in scratch copies, all killed: (1) bare git in diskState -> sentinel + no-fallback tests fail; (2) accept relative PATH entries -> case (b) + relative-only case fail; (3a) win32 miss returns 'git' -> 4 ENOENT cases fail; (3b) runGit falls back to bare git on a resolution miss -> no-fallback test fails (note: that test mocks gitExecutable, so it guards the runners, while 3a guards the resolver); (4) Windows-native bare 'git' in runGit -> both planted git.exe/git.com tests fail. Checks: resolution is lazy, never at import; resolver is sync/idempotent so concurrent first calls are harmless; hostile PATH values fail closed (half-quoted, quoted-with-semicolon, double-quoted -> ENOENT, UNC/\\?\ accepted, 1M relative entries resolved in 187 ms with 2 probes); directory named git.exe skipped via isFile; POSIX returns bare 'git' with no probes. Grep: no bare git spawn left in src outside tests EXCEPT src/benchmarks/baselineRun.ts (POSIX-only dev benchmark driver, header says so; not daemon runtime; left alone). Theoretical residuals: absolute PATH entries inside the project are still honoured; a dead UNC PATH entry could stall statSync on a git miss (miss not cached); POSIX execvp still resolves relative PATH entries against cwd (DoD says POSIX unchanged).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Reuse accounts/claudeAuth.ts findWindowsCommand: rejected.
- It keeps relative PATH entries: statSync resolves them against the daemon cwd, and the returned relative path is then resolved by libuv against the spawn cwd.
- It walks PATHEXT, so a git.cmd/git.bat is picked over a later git.exe, and Node refuses .cmd/.bat without a shell (EINVAL). Today libuv would have skipped it.
- accounts/ must stay free of daemon imports, so it cannot be moved into util/ to share.
2) Drop the spawn cwd and pass `git -C <project>`: rejected. libuv then searches the daemon's own cwd, which IS the project when the daemon is started from a terminal or wrapper (the project resolves from cwd). Relative PATH entries still resolve against it.
3) `where.exe git`: rejected, it searches the current directory first.
4) NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath: measured ineffective for libuv.
5) Route diskState through runGit's readOnlyGitEnv/readOnlyGitArgs: rejected.
- Masking global/system config (excludesFile, autocrlf) changes the `git status` change list. The equality-only signature would flap and raise false 'stale' alarms, against invariant 1.
- It would also change POSIX behaviour, which the DoD forbids.
- The task asked to 'check' this, and the decision is recorded in the defaultGitRunner comment.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Bare `git` spawn sites in the daemon:
  - util/diskState.ts:43 (defaultGitRunner; callers claimNextTask.ts:849 and releaseTask.ts:166);
  - util/cachedPlanPaths.ts:54 runGit and :76 runGitHead (callers submitPlan.ts via findCachedPlanPaths, context/repositorySource.ts, delivery/requiredChecks.ts).
  - Every other spawn uses process.execPath or the accounts CLI's resolved claude.
- CQ-R01 protectedDaemonEnvironment (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt) strips blank, relative and project PATH entries, but only for IDE-launched daemons. libuv searches the spawn cwd regardless.
- libuv uses the child env's PATH when `env` is passed (runGit). readOnlyGitEnv copies PATH unchanged, so resolving once from process.env.PATH gives the same answer. On Windows, process.env.PATH is case-insensitive.
- Test mocking:
  - cachedPlanPaths.test.ts mocks node:child_process file-wide. promisify of the mock resolves the callback's 2nd argument, so mocks call back with {stdout, stderr}.
  - Keep real-spawn tests in a file without that mock: gitExecutable.test.ts.
  - describe.runIf is already used (baselineRun.test.ts:228).
- Linux node_modules for gates: /tmp/moe-linux-daemon.3EJTl5/repo/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules (present 2026-10-26).
planningNotes.risks:
- POSIX execvp still resolves empty or relative PATH entries against the child cwd. That is out of scope by the DoD ('POSIX behaviour is unchanged'); a possible follow-up.
- Absolute PATH entries that point inside the project are still honoured. The IDE launch strips them; a terminal launch uses the user's own PATH.
- A success is cached per process, so a git moved after its first use needs a daemon restart. A miss is not cached.
- The Windows-only test needs whoami.exe and git on PATH, which is true on the dev box. CI ubuntu skips it, so the Windows-native run in step 3 is mandatory evidence.
- Do not call gitExecutable() outside the runners' try/async scope. A sync throw there would escape runGitHead's error classification or crash a caller.
- Do not change the diskState args or the signature format: stored handoff signatures must still compare equal.
- The shared checkout is dirty with peers' paths. Touch only these 5 files and report them in modifiedFiles.
